lead.title: adsilico (University of Leeds spin-out) raises £10M Series A led by PXN Ventures to test medical devices on virtual patients
lead.deck: The company uses AI to generate virtual hearts and blood vessels from anonymised scans, then simulates device performance across varied populations (age, sex, ethnicity, body size, disease). Proceeds will extend the platform to neurovascular devices (flow diverters for brain aneurysms) and grow the team from 14 to 34: an in-silico building block that can cut the cost and recruitment bias of device trials.

milestone.title: CHD wins CHF 150,000 from Venture Kick, first tranche of its seed, for MONI2, a connected belt for monitoring high-risk pregnancies
milestone.summary: The Biopôle-based startup is developing MONI2, a washable textile belt that records maternal and fetal ECG, contractions, fetal movements and fetal position, with an app for the patient and a web portal for clinicians. Prototype validation by Q2 2027, consumer version in early 2028, medical version targeting FDA clearance at end of 2029.
milestone.why: About 15% of births worldwide are high-risk: home monitoring relieves hospitals. The seed is said to be closing in October, with other private investors and a foundation already committed: a round to track before it shuts.

deal.thesis: The round (Bpifrance Amorçage Industriel, Medevice Capital and NACO reinvesting, OBRATORI, Estellior Capital) funds commercialisation of TempoTouch, an intraoperative system that tells the surgeon within moments whether the specimen contains cancer cells, to limit reoperations. Clinical trial completed at six French centres, CE mark expected in 2026: a typical raise just ahead of the regulatory catalyst.

brefsIntl.title: Coreline Soft wins FDA 510(k) for AVIEW Aorta Metrics, its chest-CT aortic analysis software
brefsIntl.summary: The software automatically segments the aorta, measures diameters by anatomical zone and produces 3D views: the company's 13th 510(k) clearance, widening its chest-CT AI portfolio in the US. A comparable for European imaging-AI vendors.

word.definition: An in silico trial replaces or complements part of real-patient trials with computer simulations run on a population of virtual patients.

parts.label: Virtual patients
parts.role: the simulated population, built from anonymised scans

parts.label: Physics model
parts.role: the engine that computes how the device behaves in the body

parts.label: Credibility file
parts.role: the evidence showing the regulator the model is reliable

how.t: Virtual anatomies (heart, vessels) are generated from scans, varying age, sex, body size or disease.
A physics model computes the implant's or device's performance on each virtual patient.
The context of use and model validation are documented, following the ASME V&V 40 framework adopted by the FDA, so the result counts in a regulatory file.

word.why: A device trial is costly and enrols few patients (often hundreds), with women under-represented. Simulation cuts cost and tests subgroups: a picks-and-shovels thesis on which adsilico just raised £10M. Limit: the FDA covers physics-based models, not standalone machine-learning models.
